tasks.short: Supervise marine maintenance technicians, inspect their work and record findings.

steps.what: Retrieve vessel maintenance instructions, repair history and open work
Assign maintenance and repair tasks to available marine technicians
Brief marine technicians on assignments and equipment-specific requirements
Supervise maintenance or repair and resolve technical questions
Inspect technicians' completed mechanical or electrical work for proper performance
Write maintenance inspection findings and outstanding corrective actions
Hand over the final work status and corrective actions to colleagues

tasks.design: Configure an equipment-indexed maintenance view in {OPS_SYSTEM}, linked to instructions in {DOCS}, and a native inspection record form. The engineer separately assigns work, briefs technicians, supervises, inspects, writes findings and communicates the final status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions and repair history are scattered, while inspection records repeat equipment and job details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native equipment views and reusable inspection fields can remove repeated clerical preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden mechanical or electrical faults require physical inspection and technical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsafe or incomplete work and direct appropriate correction.
tasks.altitude: Keep technical supervision present while making its inspection evidence easier to trace.

reach.learn: Report actual work and unresolved conditions against the correct equipment identifier.

evidence.claim: Native equipment views and inspection forms could reduce reference lookup and repeated recording; this supervision saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This maintenance-supervision scenario includes work allocation, an inspection record and a watch-status handover. No record is hidden inside the in-person inspection or briefing.

The engineer produces equipment and job identifier, inspection date, observed result, unresolved defect and corrective action in s6. Its retained seven hours include capture and checks. Unknown condition is recorded as unresolved and manually investigated.
Use existing native maintenance views and forms first. No automatic sensor inference, maintenance release, equipment actuation or external message is proposed.
Internal colleague communication stays write_internal. The record has no self-approval gate; the handover's final-status check is counted in s7.
Savings concern lookup and repeated record details, not a same-system save or reduced inspection.
unknowns: Current maintenance software, record templates and actual lookup effort.
research_questions: Does the native view and record form reduce clerical time while preserving all unresolved defects?

already_counted.description: Capture and check the inspection record.

incremental.description: Maintain equipment links and inspection fields.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final equipment status and corrective actions communicated to the engineering watch; status changes require a fresh check before handover.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 native-record scenario: B=100, R=95, gross=5; upkeep=1.5 gives central net=3.5. Supervision and inspection retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep responsibility for marine maintenance quality while improving supporting information and records.
reach: Connect technician assignments, inspection findings and watch handovers.
role.ambitious_version: A ship engineer who can trace every maintenance status to actual inspected work without reducing technical oversight.
